Wrote docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-028.md for WF02-REQ-028 (manual check-in list, door, no QR) at branch feature/WF02-REQ-028, commit 2288978. Scope test: Step 2's artifacts_out (domain/registration.ts's listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin/countCheckedIn/decideCheckinToggleOutcome/toggleCheckIn; handlers/checkin.ts's rewritten makeCheckInHandler plus new makeCheckinToggleCallbackHandler/makeCheckinPageCallbackHandler/renderCheckinListMessage; index.ts's new callback-query wiring; new checkin.* i18n keys) is real behavioral surface -- a real command/callback handler pair rendering a real Telegram inline keyboard and writing real registrations/audit_log rows. Full Steps 3b/4 apply.

Read core-directives.md, WF-02 Step 3, qa_testing_guide.md, docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-027.md as reference shape, docs/agents/design/REQ-028.md in full, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts and apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.ts (the real implementations, full reads), apps/bot/src/domain/eventStaffAuthorization.ts (unchanged, reused), and BACKEND-DEV's already-committed apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.db.test.ts in full (6 tests, one per AC1-AC6, all real bot.handleUpdate() dispatch) so this spec's own cases are independently parameterized, not duplicates. Also read handoffs/WF02-REQ-028/step-02c-security-reviewer.json in full for SECURITY-REVIEWER's two ad hoc findings this run's task brief asked to formalize.

Per-case design, all for a SECOND, NEW test file this spec designs, apps/bot/src/handlers/checkin.forgery.test.ts -- THIS FILE DOES NOT EXIST YET. Per this project's established convention (confirmed precedent: apps/bot/src/handlers/reminder24h.forgery.test.ts for REQ-026, apps/bot/src/handlers/event.dispatch.test.ts for REQ-027), TEST-DESIGNER writes the markdown design only; TEST-RUNNER writes and commits the actual vitest file at Step 4 once this design passes Step 3b. Own nextTgId=920_000_000+ range is designed to be distinct from every existing file's range (800M/900M/900M/940M/950M/950M/960M/970M/980M/990M/1000000900, confirmed via grep -rn "nextTgId = " apps/bot/src against those existing files):

- AC1: own genuinely different interleaving from both BACKEND-DEV's committed case and REVIEWER's independent re-check -- a real page-turn re-render (makeCheckinPageCallbackHandler) sits between the initial render and the stale toggle press, not a bare render-then-tap. 12-attendee/2-page fixture, target attendee lands on page 1. Proves the write-time recheck holds even after an intervening full re-render, which BACKEND-DEV's single-render case cannot expose since it never exercises the page-turn handler at all.
- AC3: own 2-attendee fixture, both with phone+email populated (BACKEND-DEV's own AC3 fixture seeds exactly one attendee), PLUS a second attendee with NO profiles row inserted at all (the noNameFallback/tgUsername-fallback path via a genuinely absent LEFT JOIN match, distinct from BACKEND-DEV's fixture which always inserts a profiles row) -- confirms the LEFT JOIN's no-match path also leaks nothing structurally.
- AC4: own before/after counter sequence driven through two real toggle writes (check-in, check-in, undo) via the handler chain rather than BACKEND-DEV's own raw-SQL UPDATE -- asserts a 4-point header sequence (0/3 -> 1/3 -> 2/3 -> 1/3) and a full-row events deep-equality before/after, proving the counter is fresh across a toggle-driven down-then-up-again sequence, not just across one out-of-band DB write.
- Cross-event forged toggle: formalizes SECURITY-REVIEWER's ad hoc finding (handoffs/WF02-REQ-028/step-02c-security-reviewer.json's "CROSS-EVENT FORGED TOGGLE") as a permanent committed regression test -- that finding was verified with a temporary test SECURITY-REVIEWER wrote, ran, and reverted via `git checkout --`, leaving zero permanent coverage before this spec. Own fixture: two events, a staff member added to Event A only, a hand-built forged checkin:toggle:<id> callback_data for an Event-B registration paired with a hand-built FakeMessage (no genuine render ever produced this pairing). Asserts the exact notAuthorized alert text (distinguished from AC1's refusedNotAdmitted alert), no write, no editMessageText, and an audit_log row with entityId = Event B's id specifically (not Event A's), which would catch a regression that authorizes against a cached/caller-supplied eventId instead of the fresh getEventIdForRegistration-derived one.
- Genuine concurrent double-toggle: a new case with no existing coverage anywhere -- two Promise.all'd bot.handleUpdate() dispatches of the IDENTICAL toggle callback fired concurrently against the same starting row, formalizing SECURITY-REVIEWER's structural "S6 CONCURRENT-TOGGLE RACE TRACE" (same handoff) as an empirically-run test. Asserts the exact predicted final state (checkedInAt === null -- check-in then immediate undo, per the trace's own reasoning about READ COMMITTED + SELECT...FOR UPDATE) and exactly one audit row of each action type (never two of either), which would catch a regression that weakens the row lock or moves the decide-then-write outside the transaction boundary (a lost-update bug would instead produce two registration.checkin audit rows and/or a race-dependent final state).

AC2/AC5/AC6 deliberately NOT re-covered: BACKEND-DEV's own committed cases for those three already drive through real dispatch with adequate own-fixture coverage per this run's task brief, and no gap was found in them while reading checkin.db.test.ts directly.

Stated the --no-file-parallelism requirement (ISS-0014) for TEST-RUNNER. No implementation defect found in domain/registration.ts's or handlers/checkin.ts's REQ-028 additions while reading them directly -- nothing to file under ISSUE_QUEUE.md from this step.
